Q: How to kill Fragment? A:

It is a old question, but for the sake of completeness, the right way is to create a method within the fragment to stop the sensor; Invoke this method before removing the fragment.

Q: TimescaleDB Hypertable Performance Slower Than Normal Table for Time-Series Queries – Why? A:

Disclaimer - I work for TigerData (creators of TimescaleDB)

Thank you for posting such a detailed and reproducible report!

You are using just one feature of TimescaleDB (autopartitioning with hypertables). Extra dimensions, however, are not needed here.

The features you are missing on:
- Columnstore/compression - ~90% of space saving + queries speedup
- Continuous Aggregates - significant speed-up for time-bucketed queries.

I've asked Clause code to use TimescaleDB best practices (using Tiger MCP server) and rework your DDL and queries. Full DDL below.

Summary of changes:
- Dropped extra dimensions, columnstore compression, and policy added.
- Continuous Aggregates Hourly → Daily → Monthly added.

Here is the summary of the benchmark (reduced to 5M rows), after applying all the Timescale best practices:

Performance & Space Savings Highlights

  Performance Improvements

  Monthly Aggregation Queries (4-year period):
  - Normal Table: 1,623 ms
  - Hypertable (compressed): 85 ms → 19x faster than normal table
  - Monthly CAGG: 0.56 ms → 152x faster than hypertable, 2,900x faster than normal table

  Key Insight: Continuous aggregates provide 100-1,000x speedups for time-series analytics queries.

  Space Savings

  Raw Data Storage:
  - Normal Table: 1,885 MB
  - Hypertable (compressed): 155 MB → 92% space reduction
  - Compression factor: 9.69x

  CAGG Hierarchy Storage:
  - Hourly: 139 MB (629K records)
  - Daily: 3.6 MB (26K records)
  - Monthly: 1.1 MB (906 records)
  - Total CAGG overhead: 144 MB (9% of compressed data)

  Combined Benefits

  Storage: 92% reduction (1,885 MB → 155 MB compressed + 144 MB CAGGs = 299 MB total)

  Query Performance: 152x speedup for aggregations while using 84% less total storage than normal tables

  The Win: Sub-millisecond queries over years of data with 6x less storage than traditional PostgreSQL tables.

Updated DDL:

-- Optimized TimescaleDB Schema using TigerData Best Practices
-- Original Source - https://stackoverflow.com/q/79849582
-- Optimized Version - 2026-01-04
-- Updated with CAGG Hierarchy: Hourly → Daily → Monthly

-- ========================================
-- HYPERTABLE with Columnstore Compression
-- ========================================
-- Using new WITH syntax instead of create_hypertable()
-- Removed space partitioning (not recommended per best practices)
-- Using columnstore compression with optimized settings

CREATE TABLE stat_flow
(
    time         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    dev_id       BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    stat_info    JSONB,
    setting_info JSONB,
    run_info     JSONB
) WITH (
    tsdb.hypertable,
    tsdb.partition_column='time',
    tsdb.enable_columnstore=true,
    tsdb.segmentby='dev_id',           -- Device ID is the primary filter dimension
    tsdb.orderby='time DESC'           -- Natural time-series ordering
);

-- Set chunk interval to 7 days (same as original)
-- This balances chunk size with 5-10 minute recording intervals
SELECT set_chunk_time_interval('stat_flow', INTERVAL '7 days');

-- ========================================
-- INDEXES on Hypertable
-- ========================================
-- Composite index for common query pattern: filtering by device and time range
CREATE INDEX idx_stat_flow_dev_id_time ON stat_flow (dev_id, time DESC);

-- ========================================
-- COMPRESSION POLICY
-- ========================================
-- Compression policy is automatically created when using enable_columnstore=true
-- No need to manually call add_columnstore_policy()

-- ========================================
-- RETENTION POLICY (OPTIONAL)
-- ========================================
-- Uncomment and adjust based on data retention requirements
-- SELECT add_retention_policy('stat_flow', INTERVAL '365 days');

-- ========================================
-- CONTINUOUS AGGREGATE HIERARCHY
-- ========================================
-- Best Practice: Create a hierarchy of continuous aggregates
-- Hourly → Daily → Monthly
-- This reduces processing overhead and improves query performance

-- ----------------------------------------
-- LEVEL 1: HOURLY AGGREGATES (from raw data)
-- ----------------------------------------
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW stat_flow_hourly
WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
SELECT
    time_bucket(INTERVAL '1 hour', time) AS bucket,
    dev_id,
    COUNT(*) as record_count,
    AVG((stat_info ->> 'temperature')::numeric) as avg_temperature,
    MIN((stat_info ->> 'temperature')::numeric) as min_temperature,
    MAX((stat_info ->> 'temperature')::numeric) as max_temperature,
    STDDEV((stat_info ->> 'temperature')::numeric) as stddev_temperature,
    AVG((stat_info ->> 'humidity')::numeric) as avg_humidity,
    MIN((stat_info ->> 'humidity')::numeric) as min_humidity,
    MAX((stat_info ->> 'humidity')::numeric) as max_humidity,
    STDDEV((stat_info ->> 'humidity')::numeric) as stddev_humidity,
    AVG((stat_info ->> 'carbon_dioxide')::numeric) as avg_carbon_dioxide,
    MIN((stat_info ->> 'carbon_dioxide')::numeric) as min_carbon_dioxide,
    MAX((stat_info ->> 'carbon_dioxide')::numeric) as max_carbon_dioxide,
    STDDEV((stat_info ->> 'carbon_dioxide')::numeric) as stddev_carbon_dioxide
FROM stat_flow
GROUP BY bucket, dev_id;

-- Refresh policy: Every 10 minutes, excluding most recent 10 minutes
SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy(
    'stat_flow_hourly',
    start_offset => NULL,
    end_offset => INTERVAL '10 minutes',
    schedule_interval => INTERVAL '10 minutes'
);

-- Compress hourly aggregates after 1 day
ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW stat_flow_hourly SET (
    timescaledb.enable_columnstore,
    timescaledb.segmentby = 'dev_id',
    timescaledb.orderby = 'bucket DESC'
);

CALL add_columnstore_policy('stat_flow_hourly', after => INTERVAL '1 day');

-- Index for efficient device + time queries
CREATE INDEX idx_hourly_dev_id_bucket ON stat_flow_hourly (dev_id, bucket DESC);

-- ----------------------------------------
-- LEVEL 2: DAILY AGGREGATES (from hourly)
-- ----------------------------------------
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW stat_flow_daily
WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
SELECT
    time_bucket(INTERVAL '1 day', bucket) AS bucket,
    dev_id,
    SUM(record_count) as record_count,
    AVG(avg_temperature) as avg_temperature,
    MIN(min_temperature) as min_temperature,
    MAX(max_temperature) as max_temperature,
    -- Note: Cannot directly aggregate stddev, using avg of hourly stddevs as approximation
    AVG(stddev_temperature) as avg_stddev_temperature,
    AVG(avg_humidity) as avg_humidity,
    MIN(min_humidity) as min_humidity,
    MAX(max_humidity) as max_humidity,
    AVG(stddev_humidity) as avg_stddev_humidity,
    AVG(avg_carbon_dioxide) as avg_carbon_dioxide,
    MIN(min_carbon_dioxide) as min_carbon_dioxide,
    MAX(max_carbon_dioxide) as max_carbon_dioxide,
    AVG(stddev_carbon_dioxide) as avg_stddev_carbon_dioxide
FROM stat_flow_hourly
GROUP BY time_bucket(INTERVAL '1 day', bucket), dev_id;

-- Refresh policy: Every 1 hour, excluding most recent 1 hour
SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy(
    'stat_flow_daily',
    start_offset => NULL,
    end_offset => INTERVAL '1 hour',
    schedule_interval => INTERVAL '1 hour'
);

-- Compress daily aggregates after 7 days
ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW stat_flow_daily SET (
    timescaledb.enable_columnstore,
    timescaledb.segmentby = 'dev_id',
    timescaledb.orderby = 'bucket DESC'
);

CALL add_columnstore_policy('stat_flow_daily', after => INTERVAL '7 days');

-- Index for efficient device + time queries
CREATE INDEX idx_daily_dev_id_bucket ON stat_flow_daily (dev_id, bucket DESC);

-- ----------------------------------------
-- LEVEL 3: MONTHLY AGGREGATES (from daily)
-- ----------------------------------------
CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW stat_flow_monthly
WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
SELECT
    time_bucket(INTERVAL '1 month', bucket) AS bucket,
    dev_id,
    SUM(record_count) as record_count,
    AVG(avg_temperature) as avg_temperature,
    MIN(min_temperature) as min_temperature,
    MAX(max_temperature) as max_temperature,
    AVG(avg_stddev_temperature) as avg_stddev_temperature,
    AVG(avg_humidity) as avg_humidity,
    MIN(min_humidity) as min_humidity,
    MAX(max_humidity) as max_humidity,
    AVG(avg_stddev_humidity) as avg_stddev_humidity,
    AVG(avg_carbon_dioxide) as avg_carbon_dioxide,
    MIN(min_carbon_dioxide) as min_carbon_dioxide,
    MAX(max_carbon_dioxide) as max_carbon_dioxide,
    AVG(avg_stddev_carbon_dioxide) as avg_stddev_carbon_dioxide
FROM stat_flow_daily
GROUP BY time_bucket(INTERVAL '1 month', bucket), dev_id;

-- Refresh policy: Every 1 day, excluding most recent 1 day
SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy(
    'stat_flow_monthly',
    start_offset => NULL,
    end_offset => INTERVAL '1 day',
    schedule_interval => INTERVAL '1 day'
);

-- Compress monthly aggregates after 30 days
ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW stat_flow_monthly SET (
    timescaledb.enable_columnstore,
    timescaledb.segmentby = 'dev_id',
    timescaledb.orderby = 'bucket DESC'
);

CALL add_columnstore_policy('stat_flow_monthly', after => INTERVAL '30 days');

-- Index for efficient device + time queries
CREATE INDEX idx_monthly_dev_id_bucket ON stat_flow_monthly (dev_id, bucket DESC);

-- ========================================
-- AGGREGATE RETENTION POLICIES (OPTIONAL)
-- ========================================
-- Aggregates are typically kept longer than raw data
-- Uncomment and adjust based on requirements
-- SELECT add_retention_policy('stat_flow_hourly', INTERVAL '90 days');
-- SELECT add_retention_policy('stat_flow_daily', INTERVAL '1 year');
-- SELECT add_retention_policy('stat_flow_monthly', INTERVAL '5 years');

-- ========================================
-- NORMAL TABLE (for comparison)
-- ========================================
-- Standard PostgreSQL table with proper indexing

CREATE TABLE stat_flow_normal
(
    time         TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    dev_id       BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    stat_info    JSONB,
    setting_info JSONB,
    run_info     JSONB
);

-- Composite indexes for efficient queries
CREATE INDEX idx_stat_flow_normal_dev_id_time ON stat_flow_normal (dev_id, time DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_stat_flow_normal_time_dev_id ON stat_flow_normal (time DESC, dev_id);

-- ========================================
-- VERIFICATION QUERIES
-- ========================================
-- Run these queries after data load to verify configuration

-- Check hypertable configuration
-- SELECT * FROM timescaledb_information.hypertables WHERE hypertable_name = 'stat_flow';

-- Check columnstore settings
-- SELECT * FROM timescaledb_information.columnstore_settings WHERE hypertable_name = 'stat_flow';

-- Check continuous aggregates
-- SELECT * FROM timescaledb_information.continuous_aggregates;

-- Check policies (compression, retention, refresh)
-- SELECT * FROM timescaledb_information.jobs ORDER BY job_id;

-- Monitor chunk information and compression stats
-- SELECT
--     chunk_name,
--     pg_size_pretty(table_size) as table_size,
--     pg_size_pretty(compressed_heap_size) as compressed_heap_size,
--     pg_size_pretty(compressed_index_size) as compressed_index_size,
--     ROUND(100.0 * compressed_heap_size / NULLIF(table_size, 0), 2) as compression_ratio_pct
-- FROM timescaledb_information.chunks
-- WHERE hypertable_name = 'stat_flow'
-- ORDER BY chunk_name DESC;

-- ========================================
-- CAGG HIERARCHY BENEFITS
-- ========================================
-- 1. Reduced Processing: Each level processes less data
--    - Hourly: Processes raw data (5M records → ~2k hourly records per device)
--    - Daily: Processes hourly aggregates (~2k → ~80 daily records)
--    - Monthly: Processes daily aggregates (~80 → ~3 monthly records)
--
-- 2. Query Performance:
--    - Hourly: Best for recent data analysis (last 7-30 days)
--    - Daily: Best for medium-term trends (last 1-12 months)
--    - Monthly: Best for long-term trends (multi-year analysis)
--
-- 3. Storage Efficiency:
--    - Each level has its own compression policy
--    - Older aggregates compress extremely well
--    - Can apply different retention policies at each level
--
-- 4. Refresh Efficiency:
--    - Hourly refreshes every 10 minutes (only processes new data)
--    - Daily refreshes every 1 hour (only processes updated hourly data)
--    - Monthly refreshes every 1 day (only processes updated daily data)
